chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who took an egg from the war booty. They said, 'He has stolen, cut off his hand.' He said, 'I have not cut off anyone's hand for what he took, as long as he had a share in it.'

key_terms.اقْطَعَهُ: Cut off his hand (standard theft punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on stealing from war booty in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) established that the hadd punishment for theft does not apply to an individual who takes from the war booty (maghnam) if they possess a co-ownership share (shirk) in it, distinguishing this from pure theft. This ruling highlights the unique legal status of maghnam in Shia jurisprudence, where the distribution process involves shared ownership before final allocation, thereby exempting individuals from the strict criteria of 'taking from another's exclusive possession' required for cutting the hand.
